finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches a user-supplied URL after only a substring check (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")). The check is bypassable, e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://example.io@evil.com/, or http://example.io.evil.com/. The default http.Get client follows redirects, so even a request to a genuine example.io-hosted URL could be redirected to an internal target. The response body is copied back to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF, not blind.
finding.source: r.FormValue("logo") (query or form parameter on /logo), main.go:31
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response body written to the client via io.Copy at main.go:38

trace.note: raw := r.FormValue("logo") takes the attacker-controlled value
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only validation; it is a substring check and does not close the finding
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects, with no scheme or host restriction
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched content to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is a substring match on the raw string. It does not parse the URL, compare .hostname against a set, restrict the scheme, block redirects, or check the resolved IP. The route is registered at main.go:43 with no authentication. Substring checks do not count as validation under the SSRF skill's rules.

verdict.guard_found: none (only strings.Contains substring check at main.go:32; no URL parsing, host allowlist, scheme restriction, or redirect blocking on /logo; the strict allowlist and noRedirect client at main.go:20-24 apply only to /cdn)
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes r.FormValue("logo") from an unauthenticated route (main.go:43), the only guard is the substring check at main.go:32, and http.Get(raw) at main.go:36 uses the default redirect-following client with the body returned via io.Copy at main.go:38.
